claim: Oil-based softgels are more effective than tablets for Vitamin D3 absorption because Vitamin D is fat-soluble and softgels provide the fat medium required for absorption.
stance_target: Briyo's softgel formulation as superior delivery format
quoted_support: Oil-based softgels often outperform tablets because they already provide a medium for absorption. This is why many experts recommend softgels, since they align better with how the body naturally processes the nutrient.

claim: Deficiency correction typically requires 2000-5000 IU of Vitamin D3 daily under medical guidance, placing Briyo's 2000 IU dose at the low end of the therapeutic correction range.
stance_target: Briyo 2000 IU dosage appropriateness for deficiency correction
scope_conditions: Vitamin D deficient individuals, under medical supervision
quoted_support: Research published in Frontiers in Endocrinology suggests that doses between 2000–5000 IU may be necessary to restore optimal levels in deficient individuals (Pludowski et al., 2018).

claim: Vitamin K2 (MK-7) should be combined with Vitamin D3 to prevent arterial calcification by directing absorbed calcium to bones rather than arteries.
stance_target: D3+K2 combination as gold standard vs. standalone D3
quoted_support: Without proper direction, calcium can accumulate in arteries instead of being deposited in bones. This is where Vitamin K2 (particularly MK-7) comes in: it activates proteins that guide calcium into bones and teeth while preventing arterial calcification.
